analysis:
This batch has two changes. (1) A new changelog fragment, changelog.d/provider-release-tag-notes.md lines 1-7, says provider release notes will be published from the tag annotation with the SSH/PGP signature block removed. The signature stays in git as verification data. (2) docs/developer/test.md changes only the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a paragraph (head lines 837-842) describing scripts/test-provider-release-publication.py. That script uses isolated local Git tags with synthetic SSH/PGP armor and checks note text and payload/provenance digest guards. It does not invoke signing or live publication.

Neither file contains executable code, so there is no runtime change to the provider, the coordinator WebSocket contract, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, the encrypted prefix cache (T-041), or the fan helper.

The actual publication-script change is outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that the signature stripping only affects published note text. It should also confirm that it does not weaken the signed-tag verification gates the docs mention at lines 827-830, namely signed tags, trusted master before secrets, and exact artifact registration. The notes are derived from tag annotations, which a tag author controls. Whether they are sanitized or escaped when rendered is also not visible here. The test.md text describes digest guards but does not show them, so I cannot confirm the guards are correct. The documentation claims are consistent with the existing threat model, which treats release publication as qualification-only and not as Apple runtime proof. No finding is raised from this evidence.
